page: Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-intel is a High Performance family server configured with 8 shared vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, the instance features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, providing 2 threads per core. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. This hardware configuration is bundled with 350 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server primarily in the average performance tier. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scored 1437.59, while the multi-core test reached 11603.93. Memory bandwidth tests show 831.82 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 62.89 GB/sec read and 44.5 GB/sec write for large uncached blocks. The server demonstrates average capabilities in static web serving at 8.38 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 12.74 million operations per second.

Performance tradeoffs are evident in multi-threaded decompression and database operations, where the bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 35.65 GB/sec and PassMark database operations at 2589.14 both register in the weak category. Additionally, LLM inference on a medium 7B model is poor, yielding only 11.11 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 5.01 tokens/sec for text generation. Given the shared CPU allocation and 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads like static web serving, basic caching, and lightweight utility computing rather than heavy database or large-scale AI tasks.
